narr: After several days of much drier conditions, a more traditional monsoon pattern returned as an area of high pressure developed near the Oklahoma and Texas border and a potent upper-level low pressure system developed off the coast of northern California. This resulted in southerly flow over New Mexico that allowed for moisture to stream back into the area. Scattered showers and thunderstorms made their return to western and central potions of the state. However, with so much dry air being in place previously, the atmosphere took time to moisten back up. Therefore, wetting rain wasn't common across much of the area. The exception was near Ruidoso on the McBride burn scar where an isolated thunderstorm resulted in flash flooding.
ev: The Lincoln County emergency manager reported Gavilan Canyon Road near Janet Drive experienced flash flooding as heavy rain fell on the McBride burn scar. Damages are not known.
lsr: BURN SCAR FLASH FLOODING AT JANET DR. AND GAVILAN CANYON ROAD WITHIN THE MCBRIDE FIRE BURN SCAR.
